meta.description: Misconception remediation paths for Stage 2 MCQs

angle_from_surface.feedback: This answer suggests the angle may have been measured from the mirror surface instead of the normal.
angle_from_surface.calm_prompt: Let's revisit the normal — angles are measured from that dashed perpendicular line.

incident_reflected_swap.feedback: This answer suggests that the incident and reflected rays may have been interchanged.
incident_reflected_swap.calm_prompt: Check the arrow direction: incident ray points toward the surface.

concave_convex_confusion.feedback: This answer suggests concave and convex mirrors may have been mixed up.
concave_convex_confusion.calm_prompt: Here is another way to see this: check which side is the reflecting surface.

F_C_confusion.feedback: This answer suggests F and C may have been confused on the principal axis.
F_C_confusion.calm_prompt: P is on the mirror; C is the centre of the sphere; F lies between P and C.

R_2f_misuse.feedback: This answer suggests R = 2f may not have been applied correctly.
R_2f_misuse.calm_prompt: F is midway between P and C when R = 2f.

real_means_erect.feedback: This answer suggests that a real image was assumed to be erect.
real_means_erect.calm_prompt: Real images from single mirrors are often inverted; virtual images are erect.

virtual_means_invisible.feedback: This answer suggests a virtual image was treated as invisible.
virtual_means_invisible.calm_prompt: Virtual means light does not actually meet there — you can still see the image.
